previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of sclerosing mesenteritis, multiple bowel resections, and chronic bowel dysmotility was admitted for acute worsening of abdominal pain above her baseline, triggered by eating a small amount of food during a period of high stress due to her husband's recent surgery. She had decreased bowel movements and uncontrolled pain despite her usual rectal Dilaudid, prompting ER presentation. During the 11-day admission, her pain was managed with IV Dilaudid and IV promethazine, with gradual improvement allowing transition back to home pain regimen. Iron deficiency anemia was identified and treated with three days of IV ferric gluconate. Her chronic right femoral central venous catheter, used for TPN, was replaced due to a crack; the procedure was successful, though it caused transient leg pain likely from superficial nerve irritation. No source of bleeding was found. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume TPN, IV fluids, and home medications, and to follow up for lab monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o woman with h/o mesenteric fibromatosis and multiple 
admissions for SBO who presented with nausea and vomiting, 
without evidence of obstruction on imaging. 
 
1. Nausea/vomiting/abdominal pain: This was consistent with her 
multiple past admissions for exacerbation of her chronic 
abdominal pain. Imaging did not demonstrate any evidence of 
bowel obstruction. She did not have any further episodes of 
vomiting. Her pain and nausea were managed with her usual 
protocol, which included morphine suppositories and IV dilaudid 
for breakthrough pain, as well as IV Phenergan for nausea. This 
regimen was confirmed with the Pain Management Clinic 
physicians, who know this patient well. Phenergan PR was also 
tried, and she seemed to feel that this improved her nausea 
better than IV. Her outpatient gastroenterologist was consulted, 
who suggested that she be managed in the usual manner with the 
aforementioned medications and that she be discharged with a 
prescription for PR Phenergan to attempt to avoid repeat 
hospitalizations for nausea. She was also treated with glycerine 
suppositories and fleet enemas for constipation. Her home TPN 
regimen was continued through her femoral line with Nutrition 
following. Initially she was NPO then advanced to clear liquids. 
She requested a regular diet around ___ and had two episodes of 
vomiting overnight several days into the regular diet. Upon 
consultation with Dr ___ was put back on clear liquids 
and discharged home on this diet. She was instructed to 
gradually advance her diet at home.

2. Mesenteric fibromatosis: Stable on her home IM Lupron depot. 
Last injection was on ___ per patient. She was continued on 
all of her home medications per the recommnedation of her 
outpatient gastroenterologist.

complain of burning pain with infusions at her R femoral TPN 
line. There was minimal surrounding erythema and no induration 
at the site. On ___ a line study was completed that showed no 
leak in the tunneled portion of the line. A tear in the outer 
portion was repaired. She was pretreated with 50 mg prednisone 
at 3 hrs and 1 hr prior to the procedure for a history of hives 
with iodinated contrast.

4. Chronic migraine headaches: Remained at her baseline, as she 
reported almost daily migraine headaches. No concerning 
neurologic signs or symptoms. She was treated with sumatriptan

5. Anemia of chronic disease: Her hematocrit remained in the

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History of mesenteric fibrosis, evaluate for small bowel
obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, most recently ___.

FINDINGS:  Supine and upright views of the abdomen demonstrate a nonspecific
bowel gas pattern without definite evidence for obstruction.  A large amount
of stool, as well as air, is seen within the rectum.  A percutaneous
gastrostomy tube is present and projects over the left upper quadrant.  A
right-side femoral central line is present with its distal tip projecting over
the inferior portion of T11.  A nerve stimulator is also noted.  Mild
degenerative changes of the hips is noted.  There are again seen multiple
abdominal clips.

IMPRESSION:  Nonspecific bowel gas pattern with a large amount of stool and
air seen within the rectum.

REPAIR OF TUNNELED CENTRAL VENOUS CATHETER AND FLOW STUDY.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with chronic abdominal pain with indwelling
G-tube and right femoral line for TPN, please assess. Pt admitted for nausea. 
Reports groin pain with Hickman infusion.

OPERATORS:  Drs. ___ (fellow) and ___ (attending
physician).  Dr. ___ was present during key moments of the procedure.

SEDATION:  None.

CONTRAST:  Sterile 20 mL Optiray 320.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  This patient who is known to our service was informed
about the procedure and placed supine on the imaging table.  While initially
attempting to inject sterile contrast material through the red lumen, leak was
noted close to the hub.  After consultation with ___, RN, it was
repaired with an appropriate kit.  Subsequently, sterile contrast material was
injected through both the lumens, and digital road-mapping images were stored.


Both lumen were studied and there was no contrast extravasation in the
tunneled portion of the catheter or at the level of the groin and no fibrin
sheath was suggested.  The catheter tubing ends just below the right atrium. 

Patient tolerated the procedure well and no immediate post-procedure
complication was seen.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated repair of the red lumen of the tunneled right
femoral venous catheter.  Uncomplicated flow study with no evidence for fibrin
sheath, or leak within the tunneled portion of the double-lumen catheter.
